title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure in the physical plant of a data center, not in a model or a software layer. Sixty-two natural-gas generators were installed and operated at the Vineland site without the permits New Jersey requires, and the state fined the operator $1.07 million under the Air Pollution Control Act. The equipment sits in the power infrastructure that supports the campus, which is the part of a deployment furthest from any algorithm and closest to a regulator.

Catching it would not have required technical instrumentation. It would have required verifying that permits existed before the generators were installed or run, which is a documentary check available at any point before operation. Detection instead came from state inspectors who visited in late July, by which time the generators were already in place and part of the campus was already in use.

What is not established is intent or knowledge, and the federal lawsuit from homeowners over noise is an allegation rather than a finding. The Cumberland County Health Department violation orders and the state penalty are the documented outcomes here, and no ruling on the lawsuit is given.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural-gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000-kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor-trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty for violating the Air Pollution Control Act is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey.

The Vineland campus is planned as a 2.6 million-square-foot complex needing 350 megawatts, enough to power a medium-size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. It has drawn complaints, including a federal lawsuit from homeowners over persistent noise and violation orders from the Cumberland County Health Department for excessive noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said data center builders must benefit New Jersey communities.
